To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

insulin receptor (IR)-B is expressed at low levels in intestinal stem and progenitor cells, highly proliferative intestinal epithelial cells, and colorectal cancer cells, and that IR-B limits cell proliferation.

the expression of insulin receptor ( IR ) isoforms is different in stem cells and tumors versus differentiated intestinal epithelium, that IR-B is reduced in highly proliferative stem cells and tumor cells, and that IR-B expression in Caco-2 CRC cells reduces proliferation and enhances biomarkers of differentiation.
insulin receptor isoform switching is a novel mechanism for regulating intestinal stem and tumor cell proliferation and differentiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of insulin receptor signaling in the intestinal epithelial stem cell niche and intestinal epithelial tumors.
understanding the mechanisms that control intestinal stem cells, the progenitor cells that they give rise to and how they are altered in cancer.
the impact of insulin and insulin-like growth factors (IGF) on the intestinal epithelum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
insulin receptor (IR)-B is a key regulator of intestinal stem cell (ISC) and tumor cell proliferation and differentiation.

the insulin receptor isoform IR-B limits proliferation in intestinal stem cells and progenitors and in differentiated intestinal epithelial cell lineages, and that IR-B expression may limit proliferation of colorectal cancer cells.

IR-B is expressed at low levels in highly proliferative intestinal stem cells and progenitors versus differentiated IECs in vivo and in vitro and that IR-B limits the proliferation of undifferentiated CRC cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

insulin receptor isoform switching occurs during intestinal stem cell and progenitor cell differentiation and in colorectal cancer and that this switching might contribute to altered insulin signaling and cell proliferation in the intestinal epithelial and cancer cells.
IR-A expression levels are increased and IR-B levels reduced in IESCs, progenitor cells, tumors and undifferentiated CRC cells.
IR-B expression in the intestinal epithelial cells and tumors is significantly lower than IR-A. IR-B expression is lower in IESCs, progenitors, and tumors compared to differentiated IECs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IR-B is a potential target for therapeutic intervention in intestinal epithelial stem and tumor cells, but not differentiated IECs.
insulin receptor isoform switching occurs in intestinal stem cells and progenitors, differentiated intestinal epithelial lineages, precancerous adenomas and cancer cells.

the insulin receptor (IR)-B isoform is reduced in intestinal stem cells and progenitors, in precancerous adenomas and in highly tumorigenic colorectal cancer cell lines, suggesting that IR-B may limit the proliferative impact of insulin in these cells.
